cases.name: Carolyn Nadine Davis
cases.narrative: On 7/31/1973, her body was discovered near Porter Creek Road on Franz Valley Road in Santa Rosa, just 3 feet from where the remains of Yvonne Lisa Weber and Maureen Louise Sterling had been recovered seven months prior. The cause of her death was strychnine poisoning 10 to 14 days before discovery. It could not be determined whether the poison had been administered to Davis by needle or by pill. Strychnine was sometimes mixed with other drugs, but an autopsy showed no trace of either heroin or amphetamines in her system. It could not be determined if she had been raped.

Semen was recovered from her body and a single gold loop earring was found at the site.

cases.name: Lori Lee Kursa
cases.about: She was a student at a Lawrence Cook Middle School in Santa Rosa, CA.
cases.narrative: On 12/14/1972, her frozen remains were found in a ravine approximately 50 feet off Calistoga Road, northeast of Rincon Valley in Santa Rosa, CA. The cause of her death was a broken neck with compression and hemorrhage of the spinal cord. She had not been raped and likely died one to two weeks prior to discovery. Authorities speculated that Kursa was kidnapped, forced into the van, stripped of her clothing, and that she opened the passenger door of the speeding vehicle in an attempt to escape her captor or captors, fell or jumped or was pushed out and broke her neck in the fall into the ravine. Her captor or captors left her by the side of the road. The broken neck would have prevented Kursa from moving, but it would have taken some time for her to die from the injury
